title: Make a daily briefing in Claude
description: Teach a learner to build a reusable /briefing command in Claude Code, run it, and schedule it every weekday at 9am.

seedFiles.calendar.md:

- 16:30  DEADLINE: submit briefing note on procurement reform

seedFiles.inbox.md:
# Inbox highlights

- URGENT — Director's office: procurement note now needed by 15:00, not 17:00
- HR: mandatory security training expires Friday
- Comms: quote requested for digital inclusion press release
- Newsletter: AI in government weekly digest

steps.narration: Open your terminal and type “claude”. This is a real Claude session — everything you're about to see is live.

steps.input: Create a slash command called /briefing that reads calendar.md, todo.md and inbox.md and gives me a punchy one-minute morning briefing: today's meetings, my top 3 priorities, and anything urgent from my inbox. Keep it under 150 words.
steps.narration: Step 1 — Ask in plain English for a reusable /briefing command. Claude writes it and saves it to .claude/commands.
Restart Claude — custom commands are loaded at startup.
Step 2 — Run /briefing. Claude reads your calendar, to-dos and inbox, and delivers your morning briefing.

steps.input: Save the exact cron line for my laptop into a new file called schedule.cron (just create that one file, don't run anything) so this briefing saves into briefings/ automatically every weekday at 9am.
steps.narration: Step 3 — Ask Claude to write the schedule: every weekday at 9am, the briefing arrives automatically.
That's it — a daily morning briefing in Claude, built in one short conversation.
